note:
George Balderston Kidd, a widower living on his own means, with a cook and a housemaid at 13 Newcastle Drive (#214) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the three was in the record, and 13 Newcastle Drive held only 1921, so 1891 is free.

**He held the house for at least twenty-three years, and the directory gives him a degree.** Wright's prints 'Mr. George B. Kidd' at 13 Newcastle Drive in 1894-95 and 1898-99, then 'Kidd George Balderston LL.D' in 1910-11 and 'Kidd George Balderston LL.B' in 1913-14. The two degree letters disagree between volumes, so neither is entered on his record; it is noted so that whichever is right can be added from a better source.

The only Kidd in the record is Annie Sarah Kidd (#1348, born 1861), who has a 1921 census and no property; nothing connects her to this household, so no link is made. Annie M Newbod's surname is entered as transcribed and is probably Newbold - the record holds a Newbold family in the Park - but nothing here identifies her among them, so she is created as she is written. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 13 Newcastle Drive, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 101 (Leicester Special Collections id 164607); 1898-99, page 109 (id 165285); 1910-11, page 145 (id 165821); 1913-14, page 163 (id 166519).
